answer: Use the `capabilities` command: `show capabilities-<name>`, where `name` is the name of the card (string, no default). It retrieves the capability information for that card. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For type-level (rather than instance-level) capability data, the companion commands are `show supported-card-<card-type>`, `show supported-port-<card-type>/<port-name>`, `show supported-slot-<chassis-type>/<slot-name>` and `show supported-tom-<card-type>/<port-name>/<tom-type>`.

Provisioning uses `add card-<name> required-type <value> chassis-name <value> slot-name <value>`; those three are mandatory. `required-type` is a String (length 0..32) from the supported list (BAXOFP2, BLANK, BLANK2, CAD10A, CHM1R, CHM2T, CHM6, CHM7, CHM7X, FAN, FAN-CTRL, FRCU, IOPANEL, PEM, RD20TM, SPN2, SPN2C, UCM4, UTM2, XMM4 and others). `chassis-name` is String 1..255, default 1; `slot-name` is a String. Optional on add: required-subtype, card-mode, subslot-name (settable only at creation), power-profile, alias-name, admin-state (default unlock), alarm-report-control (default inhibited), label. Example: `add card-1-4 required-type CHM1R chassis-name 1 slot-name 2`.

On 1830 GX G40 you must set the chassis ambient temperature to 40C before a Native ZR TOM will come up. If `configured-ambient-temperature` is not set, the system raises a port config mismatch alarm and the TOM cannot be provisioned. Set it with `set chassis-<name> configured-ambient-temperature 40` (the value is a number in Celsius units, no default), or supply it on `add chassis-<name>`. The attribute is the configured ambient temperature for the chassis and is used to compute the FRU's power consumption. It is readable with `show chassis-<name> configured-ambient-temperature`.

Use `set console-<name> baud-rate <value>` / `show console-<name> [baud-rate] [actual-baud-rate] [auto-sensing-state]`. Permitted values are auto-sensing, 9600, 19200, 38400, 57600 and 115200. The default is 9600 in 1830 GX G30 and 115200 in 1830 GX G40. Yes, it can work it out itself: with `auto-sensing` the system auto-detects the baud rate from 'ENTER' presses on the serial console client side, then locks it and reports it in `actual-baud-rate`. `auto-sensing-state` (visible only when auto-sensing is enabled) is sensing or locked, default sensing. Not all cards support auto-sensing; check `console-port-support` in `show supported-card`.

Use `show controller-card-<name> [redundancy-status] [redundancy-standby-status] [number-of-switchover-events] [time-of-last-switchover] [additional-details]`. `redundancy-status` is active, standby or not-in-service (default not-in-service). `redundancy-standby-status` tells you readiness: ready-synchronized (standby is in sync and ready), not-ready-synchronizing (synchronizing data with the active controller), not-ready-synchronize-fail, lock-out (protection in lock-out state), card-not-present; the default is not-ready-synchronizing. `number-of-switchover-events` (uint32) and `time-of-last-switchover` are visible only on the active controller card. `additional-details` is a string 0..128 with synchronization status detail.

Use `show equipment [<option>]`, which displays installed equipment information; access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. With no option it lists everything; supply an equipment option to narrow it to one item, for example `show equipment card-1-1`. Available options vary according to the installation. The output for a card lists its child objects (controller-card, console, ports) plus required-type, required-subtype, category, chassis-name, slot-name, max-power-draw, last-reboot-reason, alias-name, AID, admin-state, oper-state, avail-state, alarm-report-control and label.

Both are controlled by `set equipment-policies` / `show equipment-policies`. `tom-auto-migration` (enabled/disabled) enables automatic update of the TOM subtype based on the present equipment; it affects TOM subtype migration only, not TOM type migration (for example no update between QSFPDD and QSFP28), and the update may directly impact existing configurations. Per-port behavior is reported by `allows-auto-migration` in `show supported-port`. `auto-assigned-degrees` (enabled/disabled) enables automatic degree assignment when a card that supports degrees is provisioned; it defaults to disabled, but enabled if l0-mode-op is hsc-ols. Related: `auto-assigned-directions`, default enabled.

You must enable it. `set equipment-templates use-serdes-templates <value>` / `show equipment-templates use-serdes-templates` controls whether serdes-templates are globally enabled; values are enabled and disabled (the CLI value completion shows false / true) and the default is disabled. On enabling, templates are not applied retroactively; they are applied from that moment onward. On disabling there is no impact: existing serdes configuration is kept on all TOMs, whether it was applied via template or manually. Application of serdes-templates depends on this flag being 'true'; you can force re-application with the `apply-template` command.

Use `show fru-info-<manifest-file>/<equipment-type>`. This displays the packaged FRU information associated with a particular equipment-type. `manifest-file` is the manifest file, a string of length 0..256; `equipment-type` is the type of the equipment, a string of length 0..32. Neither has a default. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. This is packaged (shipped) data keyed by equipment type, as distinct from `show inventory-<name>`, which reports the data read from a FRU that is actually present.

Use the `inventory` command, which shows inventory data for a present FRU: `show inventory-<name> [serial-number] [clei] ...`. `serial-number` is the serial number of the equipment (String) and `clei` is the Common Language Equipment Identifier (String). The AID forms accepted are `inventory-<name>`, `inventory-<chassis-name>-<slot-name>`, `inventory-<card-name>-<port-name>` and `inventory-<card-name>.<slot-name>`. Other attributes on the same command include hardware-version, actual-type, actual-subtype, sw-support-revision, PON, vendor, part-number, manufacture-date, insertion-date, number-of-lanes, vendor-compliance-code, actual-power-class, actual-max-power-draw and fw-status. Example: `show inventory-1-3-1`.

Use `show led-<location>/<name> [status]` or `show leds`. The object exists even if the FRU is not physically present. `location` is the AID of the equipment location of the LED (chassis, card or port AID), String 1..32; `name` is the LED name within the FRU, String 1..16. `status` values are: not-available, off, yellow, flashing-yellow, green, flashing-green, red, flashing-red, cycling-with-off, cycling (all supported colors excluding off, used for lamp test), amber and flashing-amber. The default is not-available. Flashing states alternate between off and the named color.

In 1830 GX G40 there are three families of ports: comm-eth, USB and trib/line. comm-eth and USB ports exist on XMMs only and are found on Slot 1 XMMs. The trib/line ports appear on a CHM6 or CHM7 (slots 4-7) only after a TOM is present/provisioned in the CHM6/CHM7. Port objects are managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. The `port-type` attribute reported by `show port-<card-name>-<port-name> port-type` takes: line (line-side colored CWDM/DWDM module), tributary (grey client interfaces), tributary-subport, usb, comm, uplink, optical, otdr, pluggable (the L0 module cage for a QSFP/SFP/SFP+ TOM) and ocm.

Use `show resources-<name> [internal-cell-switch-total-bandwidth] [internal-cell-switch-available-bandwidth] [paired-slot-total-bandwidth] [paired-slot-available-bandwidth]`. The internal cell-switch attributes apply only to SPN2/SPN2C cards and default to 600.000 Gbit/s if the card has paired slot interconnection capability. The paired-slot attributes apply only to SPN2/SPN2C cards that support Paired Slots: they default to 0 if the card has no paired slot interconnection capability, and 500.000 Gbit/s if it does. The same command also shows supported-carriers, unassigned-carriers and supported-sub-components. Example: `show resources-254-1`.

Read the `status` attribute of the serdes object: `show serdes-<card-name>-<port-name>/<serdes-name> [value] [status]`. `status` is the state of the advanced parameter as observable on the system once configured, with values: set (parameter set), unknown (parameter unknown), in-progress (parameter in progress), failed (parameter failed) and not-supported (parameter not supported). The default is unknown. `value` is the parameter value (string). A plain `show serdes` lists every serdes with its value and status, for example `serdes-1-7-T1/TxEQ 1 set`. Serdes entries are managed with add/set/show/delete.

Scope is by TOM part number, card type and port list. serdes-templates are created per `tom-part-number` (string, length 1..16) and apply to all line cards that support serdes; when a TOM with that part-number is plugged in, the template is automatically applied. `ports-applicable` narrows the list of ports: values are 'all' (the default, all ports considered) or port names as strings of length 1..16, up to a maximum of 20 elements. Syntax: `add serdes-template-<name> [tom-part-number <value>] [card-types-applicable <value>] [ports-applicable <value>]`. Manual serdes configuration is still allowed and is kept even if it deviates from the template. Swapping in a TOM with a different part-number resets the serdes configuration and re-applies the new template if one exists. Application depends on `use-serdes-templates` being 'true'.

Each entry is a serdes parameter name plus its value, added under the parent template: `add serdes-template-entry-<serdes-template-name>/<serdes-template-entry-name> value <value>`. Edit with `set serdes-template-entry-<...>/<...> [value <value>]`, remove with `delete`, and read with `show serdes-template-entry-<serdes-template-name>/<serdes-template-entry-name>/<name> [value]`. `name` is the name of the serdes parameter, a string of length 0..256; `value` is the value of the serdes parameter, a string of length 0..256; `tom-part-number` is the TOM part-number the template applies to, string 1..16. Example: `add serdes-template-entry-T-DQ4CNT-NIN/RxEQ value 3`.

Yes. `set serial-console [global-switch <value>] [global-timeout <value>]` / `show serial-console [global-switch] [global-timeout]` set the global configuration of all serial console ports in the system. `global-switch` allows access by serial console; values enabled and disabled, default enabled, and each console port can override this global behavior. `global-timeout` is the serial console inactivity timeout, a number in minutes, default 60; it can be set to zero to disable the inactivity timer. The object is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Example: `set serial-console global-switch enabled global-timeout 80`. Per-card override is `set console-<name> local-switch` (use-global-switch, force-enable, force-disable).

Use `show slot-<chassis-name>-<slot-name> [AID] [supported-type] [installed-type] [oper-state] [avail-state] [current-equipment]` (or `show slot-<card-name>.<slot-name>` for a subslot). `installed-type` is the currently installed type, `supported-type` the list of types the holder accepts, and `current-equipment` the name of the equipment currently required in this slot (for example 1-1). `oper-state` is enabled or disabled, default disabled. A plain `show slot` lists every slot in the node. For what a slot type can hold before anything is installed, use `show supported-slot-<chassis-type>/<slot-name> possible-card-types` (list of up to 15 elements).

Use `show sub-component-<card-name>/<sub-component-name> [AID] [description]`; a plain `show sub-component` lists them all. `card-name` is the name of the card supporting the sub-component (string 0..64), `sub-component-name` is the sub-component name (string), `AID` is the Resource Access Identifier (string 1..64) and `description` is a user configurable description (string 0..128). Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example output: `sub-component-1-6/dco-oec`, AID 1-6-dco-oec, 'DCO OEC (Optical Engine Controller) sub-component'. The set of sub-components on a card is also reported by `show resources-<name> supported-sub-components`, which can be addressed for operations such as restart.

Use `show supported-card-<card-type> node-type-compatibility`. Node Type Compatibility refers to the supported NE node-type for a sled card, and is only of relevance for line-card(s) and carrier-card(s). The values are: all (compatible with any node-type), ILA (compatible with the In-Line Amplifier, two-directions node type) and OADM (Optical Add/Drop Multiplexer node type). So a card usable on an in-line amplifier node reports all or ILA. The same command also reports sw-support-revision, supported-subtype, description, default-card-mode, supported-card-mode, card-width, card-height, is-field-replaceable, category, grid-mode-support, max-power-draw, leds, location-led-support, console-port-support, default-console-baud-rate, support-serdes-config, supported-bands and supported-features.

Use `show supported-chassis-<chassis-type> [controller-redundancy-supported] [number-of-front-slots] [number-of-rear-slots]`. `controller-redundancy-supported` is true or false and says whether that chassis type supports controller redundancy. `number-of-front-slots` and `number-of-rear-slots` are uint8 counts of equipment holder slots in the front and back plates. chassis-type is an identityref such as G31, G32, G34c or G42. For example G42 reports controller-redundancy-supported true, 7 front slots and 12 rear slots. The same command reports supported-subtype, default-subtype, description, power-control-supported, fan-adjustment-on-altitude (default false), dust-filter-replacement (default optional-dust-filter), depth in mm, height in RUs, leds, supported-subchassis-type (max 10 elements) and supported-features.

Use `show supported-port-<card-type>/<port-name> [port-type] [configuration-mode] [faceplate-label] [allows-auto-migration] ...`, for example `show supported-port-CHM1R/2`. `port-type` says what the port is for: line, tributary, tributary-subport, usb, comm, uplink, optical, otdr, pluggable or ocm. `configuration-mode` says who configures it: system-configured (the system configures the card in the slot or TOM in the port and the user cannot make changes) or user-configured (the user can provision or de-provision). Also available: direction (not-applicable, tx, rx, rxtx), faceplate-label (1..36), leds (max 10), present (always or in-node-controller-only, default always), default-tom (default none), parent-port, subport-list and allows-auto-migration (true/false, default true).

Use `show supported-slot-<chassis-type>/<slot-name> [possible-card-types] [requires-blank-when-empty] ...`. `requires-blank-when-empty` states whether the slot needs a BLANK filler card when empty; values are not-applicable, optional and required. On a G42, the card slots 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and the PEM slots report required, while the IOPANEL, FAN and FANCTRL slots report not-applicable. `possible-card-types` lists the card types allowed in that slot, up to 15 elements (for example CHM6,UCM4 on G42 slots 4-7). The command also reports slot-location (front/rear), slot-vertical-position, slot-horizontal-position, configuration-mode, auto-provision-capable, default-card, reset-power (W at 55 degrees C), virtual-slot (default false) and leds.

Use `show supported-tom-<card-type>/<port-name>/<tom-type>/<tom-subtype-group> [supported-subtype] [supported-phy-modes] [default-phy-mode]`. It displays capability information for a supported TOM in the scope of a particular card. `supported-phy-mode` lists the phy-modes supported for that TOM on that card and `default-phy-mode` the one used by default; the values are 100GE, 200GE, 400GE, 2x100GE, 4x100GE, 100G, 4x10G, 4x10GE, 1GE, 2G5, 10G, 10GE, 2G5E, 40GE, 40G, 4x100G and 200G. `tom-type` is the form factor (for example CFP2-DCO, QSFP28, QSFPDD) and `tom-subtype-group` is a string 0..32 such as '4x100GE-breakout'. Examples: `show supported-tom-CHM1R/6/QSFP28` and `show supported-tom-CHM1R/6/QSFPDD/2x100GE-breakout`.

Use `show supported-tom-power-<card-type>/<port-name>/<tom-type> [supported-power-class] [supported-max-power-draw]`. `supported-power-class` is the maximum MSA power class the host port supports for that pluggable type, a uint8 in the range 1..8 (the port may only partially support that class, so check supported-max-power-draw). `supported-max-power-draw` is the maximum power in watts the host port allows for that pluggable type under supported-power-class, a decimal64. `tom-type` is the pluggable form factor identity matching the TOM required-type (for example CFP2-DCO, QSFP28, QSFPDD). What the installed module actually reports is read with `show inventory-<name> actual-power-class actual-max-power-draw`, which is populated only for third-party transceiver subtypes on hosts that enforce power-class rules.
